about: What a clean target needs to become the Avrana Party appliance as this commit describes it (AVR-32). Read by avrana.ops.rebuild (plan, apply, verify) and pinned to the repository by tests/unit/test_ops_rebuild.py. It is source, not proof of installation: docs/SYSTEM.md says what is deployed. By owner decision (AVR-32, 2026-10-05) the target is the ADR 0016 phase-1 architecture: the layout the unit files in source describe (dedicated service users, code under /opt), which has never run on the Pi. It is not a description of today's appliance; every recorded difference is a reconciliation item in docs/runbooks/rebuild.md ('Reconciliation with today's appliance'). The rebuild is never run on the production appliance; the owner-run read-only checks of 'unknowns' (U1-U13) and a first supervised run on a spare card are validation gates, none of them passed. No secret, key, passphrase or certificate is in this file: 'secrets' names where each one lives and who provisions it.

confidence_levels.scripted: an installer or unit in this repository names it

confidence_levels.derived: a script or unit in this repository needs the command or path; the package name or mode is this file's reading and is not confirmed on the device

management.addressing: DHCP lease from the home router

guard.about: apply and restore refuse a host that looks like an appliance this tool did not build: any of these units enabled or active, or any of these paths present, and no valid marker. The first apply on a host with none of them must name the machine (--target-hostname) and writes the marker before anything else; `seal` ends the build, after which the host is refused like any appliance. The owner override never applies while one of these units is enabled or active. Today's Pi has most of them (docs/SYSTEM.md, docs/runbooks/service-users-migration.md, docs/runbooks/party-https.md): moving it to this layout is the service-users migration, never this tool.

artifacts.provision: As the operator account: git clone the Party repository to /home/cody/avrana-party and check out the reviewed commit, detached.

The Pi's GitHub key does not read the private Games repository: carry a git bundle from a development machine and clone it (docs/runbooks/games-fork-deploy.md, section 1), then check out the reviewed commit, detached.
Built by the same ops/deploy.sh run as party-release.
sudo bash /home/cody/avrana-party/ops/install-party-web.sh /home/cody/avrana-party   # a first deploy.sh run at an unchanged checkout builds no web release

sudo python3 -m venv /opt/avrana-party-games/venv && sudo /opt/avrana-party-games/venv/bin/pip install -r /opt/avrana-party-games/current/requirements.txt   # needs the internet over eth0; root-owned, not group- or world-writable

sudo install -D -o root -g root -m 0644 <your copy of mame2010_libretro.so> /opt/avrana-arcade/cores/mame2010_libretro.so   # not in Git; keep a copy of the one on the Pi, compare its sha256 with arcade/evidence/selected-core.json
Copy your own Gauntlet II set to /srv/avrana/roms/arcade/gaunt2.zip, readable by avrana-arcade. Never downloaded, never committed; arcade/README.md records its sha256.
Install the lego ACME client as /usr/local/bin/lego (0755 root). The repository records neither its version nor where the Pi's copy came from.

secrets.provision: sudo bash /home/cody/avrana-party/ops/provision-party-game-key.sh bluff   # generated on the device, never printed

On the device only: issue party.avrana.net with lego DNS-01 into /var/lib/avrana-party/lego (docs/runbooks/party-https.md, 'Trust and key custody'; the exact lego command line used on 2026-09-25 is recorded nowhere, U13), then sudo /usr/local/libexec/avrana-party/install-party-certificate.sh <fullchain> <key>. The private key and the ACME account never leave the device.
Optional (automatic renewal): the owner writes CF_DNS_API_TOKEN and ACME_EMAIL into /etc/avrana-party/cloudflare.env on the device, root 0600. Without it renewal is manual.

The owner creates the access point profile with nmcli (python3 -m avrana.ops.rebuild ap-profile prints the command without the passphrase) and types the passphrase at NetworkManager's prompt. It is stored only in /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/ on the device.
The owner's SSH public key for the operator account, and the device's own GitHub key that reads the Party repository. Neither is in the repository.

hardware_checks.check: A phone that has forgotten the network joins "Avrana Party" with the passphrase and gets an address in 10.42.0.10-254; an iPhone shows no captive popup.
On that phone, https://party.avrana.net/party/ opens with no certificate warning (the name resolves only on the party network).
Two phones Join; the first is the Party Host; a reload keeps each phone's identity.
The Host starts BLUFF, then EXPO: the other phone follows, both play, the Host ends the game and both return to Party Home.

The Host starts Gauntlet II: video and sound arrive, two phones control two heroes, End returns everyone home. The arcade unit's hardening has never met RetroArch on any host: read its journal first if this fails.
After a power cycle with eth0 unplugged the access point, DNS and every service come back by themselves and the checks above still pass.
http://10.42.0.1/ on a phone shows the link to the Party and never redirects to HTTPS.
